statements.t: Based on its current forecast, Cummins expects revenue growth of approximately 10% compared to our prior guidance of 10% to 13%.

Cummins plans to continue generating strong operating cash flow and returns for shareholders and is committed to our goal of returning 50% of operating cash flow back to shareholders.

Our outlook reflects the following positive trends and challenges to our business that could impact our revenue and earnings potential in 2026.
• We expect demand within markets served by our Power Systems business to remain strong, including the power generation and industrial markets.
• We anticipate our aftermarket business will remain stable, driven primarily by demand in our Engine and Power Systems businesses.
• We expect strong demand for medium-duty and heavy-duty trucks in North America to continue for the remainder of 2026.
While we anticipate these actions will gradually improve the cost structure, we expect ongoing investments in priority technologies to result in continued near-term operating losses.
As a result, we do not anticipate any local liquidity restrictions to preclude us from funding our operating needs with local resources.
We intend to maintain credit facilities at the current or higher aggregate amounts by renewing or replacing these facilities at or before expiration.
We intend to use the net proceeds from the commercial paper borrowings for general corporate purposes.
We continue to invest in new product lines and targeted capacity expansions.
We plan to spend an estimated $1.35 billion to $1.45 billion in 2026 on capital expenditures with approximately 60 percent of these expenditures expected to be invested in North America.
We intend to repurchase outstanding shares from time to time during 2026 to enhance shareholder value.
We anticipate making additional defined benefit pension contributions during the remainder of 2026 of $12 million for our U.S. and U.K. qualified and non-qualified pension plans.
